answers.core:
My first thought was to add this as an add-on. However, to add this feature I need to either make a child class of `Gradient` that overrides the `get_color_at_offset` method or create a new class exactly like `Gradient` but with a different implementation of `get_color_at_offset`.

The first option would need the method to be virtual, and since it isn't, it would need to make changes to the `gradient.h` file, thus modifying the engine directly. It would then be more direct and easier to just directly add the feature directly into the `Gradient` class

The second option can be done as an add-on, but it has the main flaw of having the new class inherit from `Resource` instead of `Gradient`, making it unusable as a classic gradient with core objects.

I didn't find any other option and since it is a basic feature, I think making it a core feature would improve the engine for people who make 2D and UI-based applications.
answers.workaround: It can be worked around by making a custom gradient shader with dithering. It is however not convenient to use with themes and other shaders, making this solution convenient only for simple cases such as a background or a square texture with a gradient applied on it.
